sentences.text: Plotosaurus possessed several marine adaptations not seen in other mosasaurs, including narrower flippers, a large tail fin, and an aerodynamic fusiform body. These traits likely allowed it to be a faster swimmer than other mosasaurs, indicating more advanced swimming adaptations than its relatives.
The immature holotype of Plotosaurus had a 46 cm skull and was estimated to be 4.2 meters long in total.
One specimen of Plotosaurus was estimated to reach nearly 8 meters in length and weigh around 1654 kg.

Charles Lewis Camp described Plotosaurus in 1942 based on fossil specimens found in California, USA. The earliest specimens of Plotosaurus were found in the Moreno Formation along the San Joaquin Valley, California, in the early 20th century. Allan Bennison discovered a partial Plotosaurus skeleton near Pacheco Pass in 1937. The type species, P. bennisoni, was named by fossil collector Allan Bennison who discovered the first remains in 1937.

Plotosaurus is classified within the subfamily Mosasaurinae. Based on cladistic analyses, Plotosaurus is considered the most derived branch of mosasaur evolution. Its parent group is Mosasaurini. It belongs to the family Mosasauridae. It is classified in the class Reptilia.

It is debated whether Plotosaurus had a wider distribution beyond North America, as fragmentary specimens from Japan may belong to the genus. A fossil from Chile initially identified as Plotosaurus-like was reidentified in 2019 as possibly belonging to Halisaurus because it did not match Plotosaurus diagnostics.
